title: Geo dual-operational handoff for persistent streams and API continuity
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Objective:
Design and implement a geo-aware active-active handoff mechanism for long-lived/streaming connections and in-flight requests so hosted API traffic can be shifted across regions with minimal disruption and without requiring customers to rebuild stateful session logic. This ticket covers the control-plane changes, gateway behavior, connection token scheme, basic KV cache migration hints, SLO targets, circuit-breaker thresholds, load-shedding policy, and a staged rollout plan.

Background / motivation:
- Customers using streaming features (server-sent events, gRPC streams, WebSockets) and sessionful chat expect continuous streams even during regional maintenance or partial outages.
- Current edge gateways are stateless by design; long-lived connections terminate on region failover causing perceptible UX disruptions and amplified retry storms.
- We need a production-safe, incremental approach that preserves latency SLOs, reduces token-cost replays, and gives predictable behavior for both short-request and persistent-stream traffic.

SLOs & success metrics (target):
- API success rate (5xx < 0.05%) across regions for steady-state traffic.
- P95 generation latency <= 150ms; P99 <= 400ms for non-streaming requests under normal load.
- Streaming continuity: no more than 0.1% of active streams dropped during a weighted region shift (canary gating), and <0.5% during full region failover.
- Time-to-recover for in-flight stream reattachment < 6s for supported clients (with auto-reattach tokens).
- Safe fallbacks: when shedding is required, critical calls (priority: auth, billing, control-plane) remain <= 1% error budget.

Design overview (high-level):
1) Connection handle & short-lived reattach token:
   - On stream establishment the gateway issues a cryptographic short-lived reattach token (RAT) signed by the region control plane. Token encodes: connection id, originating shard, model variant, KV-cache-hash, expiry.
   - RATs are usable across regions if a corresponding key-rotation map exists; cross-region reattach is permitted only during controlled handoffs.

2) Sticky-hint + stateless reattach flow:
   - Primary routing remains hash-based (x-redwood-session-hash) for performance. Gateways emit a sticky-hint header to clients that can be used to prefer the originating region.
   - On handoff, controller flips region routing policy for a customer-id key range and broadcasts a handoff epoch. New connections go to target region.
   - Active streams receive a control-plane-driven push: brokered reattach instructions (via gateway-to-gateway control channel or via client reattach using RAT). Clients should attempt reattach using RAT and a short exponential backoff.

3) KV cache continuity (best-effort):
   - We will not attempt live state migration for large KV caches. Instead implement cache-hint propagation: gateways send a compact KV-cache-hash and a list of hot prefixes for the reattaching region to prefill caches asynchronously.
   - Hot-prefix prewarm service will warm the target nodes using low-priority prefetch jobs to reduce cold-start token costs.

4) Circuit breakers and load-shedding policy:
   - Circuit breakers operate at gateway and node level. Triggers: CPU>80% sustained for 30s, request queue-latency p95>200ms, active-streams/node>1200.
   - When triggered: 1) mark node degraded, 2) apply per-customer fair-share shedding, 3) reject non-critical low-priority requests with 429 + Retry-After and explicit reason header (x-redwood-shed-reason).
   - Streaming prioritization: active streams are weighted vs short requests. If load is extreme, shed new streaming starts before dropping existing streams (configurable per-customer).

5) Failover behavior and graceful degradation:
   - Canary handoff uses staged traffic shift: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health gates at each stage (5m steady-state).
   - For unplanned failover, automatic cross-region promotion uses last-known RPO: controller issues emergency handoff epoch; gateways signal clients to reattach.
   - If reattach fails, client receives a human-readable error and a suggested fallback: switch to short-polling endpoints or use a lightweight model variant.

Implementation tasks (non-exhaustive):
- Control plane: epoched routing policy API, handoff orchestration controller, RAT signing/verification (security: rotate keys monthly).
- Gateway: RAT minting/validation, reattach endpoint, prewarm hint emitter, enhanced metrics (active streams, reattach rate, RAT failures).
- Prewarm service: consume cache-hints and schedule background prefetch jobs to target region nodes.
- Client docs + SDK: reattach logic (auto-try), backoff policy, header expectations, example code for gRPC/WebSocket clients.
- Rollout automation: canary scheduler that gradually shifts prefix ranges and monitors health gates.

Acceptance criteria (must be met for Done):
- Design doc reviewed and approved by Eng+PM+SRE (link below).
- End-to-end integration tests that simulate region outage and verify reattach within 6s for 95% of simulated clients.
- Circuit breaker and load-shed policies implemented and covered by integration tests.
- Dashboard in Console showing: reattach success rate, average reattach time, active streams by region, RAT failure rate, shed events.
- Runbook added to runbooks/playbooks and an on-call drill executed successfully in staging.
- PRs merged and release notes published.

Docs and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Geo+Dual+Operational+Handoff+Design
- Implementation PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 (control-plane), https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/678 (gateway changes)
- Canary dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/hand-off/geo-handoff-canary

Open trade-offs and unresolved questions:
- Full live KV migration vs prewarm: we are choosing prewarm to reduce complexity and risk. Trade-off: initial tokens may be slightly more expensive after handoff.
- RAT cross-region validity window: security wants short TTL (30s) while UX prefers longer (60-90s) to allow slower reconnects. Proposal: 45s TTL with automatic refresh for connected clients.
- How to handle third-party proxies that terminate WebSocket and do not forward RAT headers: document and provide server-side fallback (sticky-cookie) for browser clients.

Next steps:
- Finish control-plane prototype and gateway auth flow (Marco).
- Security review with keys team for cross-region signing map (Saket).
- QA create chaos tests (network partition, delayed packet loss, partial region CPU spike).

Estimated effort by area:
- Control-plane orchestration: 3 dev-weeks
- Gateway + reattach flow: 3 dev-weeks
- Prewarm service: 2 dev-weeks
- Docs/tests/dashboards: 1.5 dev-weeks

Notes:
- This ticket intentionally scopes to the minimum required to guarantee customer continuity for streaming workloads. Follow-up tickets will iterate on cache migration fidelity and advanced reassembly protocols.
